result:
What I found, working through the current onboarding code and docs against Daniel's proposal:

**1. The first ten minutes gets cleaner, not emptier — and less needs to change than the note suggests.**

Days 1 and 2 of the current opening (harvest → plant → water → sleep, then repeat with a swipe-chained row and the hoe) already never touch gold or the shop — that's stated outright in the onboarding design ("No shop" is one of the things day 1 deliberately withholds). The shop only enters once the seed pouch runs dry, which the design notes place around day 3–4, as a two-step lesson: sell a crop, then spend the coins on three seeds.

Making a harvest itself replantable removes that two-step lesson from the must-teach path entirely, rather than just delaying it — a pre-reader who can already replant what she grew has no reason to ever see a coin, a price, or a shop screen in the opening days. That's one fewer screen and one fewer new verb inside the exact window the game measures for the pre-reader gate. It also collapses "crop becomes coins becomes three new seeds" (two hops, a number, a multiplication) into "crop becomes seed" (one hop, nothing to count) — a shorter causal chain for the same lesson, which is a straight improvement for a pre-reader.

One thing worth knowing: the onboarding design already considered exactly this model by name — "a harvest yields a seed as well as a crop" — and turned it down, on the grounds that the existing sell-then-buy economy was worth teaching for its own sake. Daniel's note reopens that specific, already-argued decision. That reversal needs to be written back into the design docs, not just built — I'm not the owner of that chapter and haven't touched it.

The mechanism itself (a harvest count feeding a plantable stock directly, with a per-person cap of 5–10 before anything becomes sellable) is a simulation-layer change: today seeds and crops are two separate stocks connected only by buying and selling, and that split is the thing that would need to merge. That's not mine to build.

**2. It doesn't need to be a letter, and this half isn't actually a ruling.**

Whatever tells the player something new has arrived can be entirely wordless, using vocabulary the game already ships: a locked object drawn as the same picture, darkened, that lights up the moment it's earned (already built for the shop), and a single glowing highlight on the thing that just became usable (the same mechanism that has taught every verb in the opening days). Nothing about "you now have this" requires a sentence — the studio has already solved harder versions of this exact problem without one.

The one part of this that is genuinely his: whether he wants an actual written note to exist anywhere as flavor — a supplier's voice, some personality — even though nothing mechanical needs it. That's a tone choice about content a player sees, not a mechanical requirement, so I'm flagging it rather than deciding it.

**3. On teaching the storage cap** (the brief cut off here, so I'm answering what I could reconstruct: what signals "you're full, time to sell"): the HUD already has almost exactly this. The basket display caps out visually at five pips and stops counting past that — "past five, lots is the honest reading" is the comment already in the code. That's the same number Daniel guessed for the early-game excess threshold. The natural move is to point that same full-basket state at the new sell trigger once the excess number is settled, rather than building a second gauge.

**What I didn't do:** I didn't touch the simulation layer, the design docs, or the HUD code — this was reading, and the actual seed/crop merge and the storage-tier numbers aren't settled yet, so there's nothing safe to build against.

follow_ups.title: Write the design note reversing the sell-then-buy economy
follow_ups.first_action: Update the onboarding chapter's rejected-fork note and record the storage-tier numbers (on-person cap, what a silo raises it to) in the design docs and decision log
follow_ups.why: Daniel's proposal reopens a fork the docs already argued against by name; the reversal has to land in the docs before anyone builds against it.

follow_ups.title: Merge seed and crop stock so a harvest is directly plantable
follow_ups.first_action: Replace the two separate seed/crop dictionaries with one plantable/sellable stock per crop type, capped at the on-person excess threshold, and re-check the existing no-soft-lock proof against the new model since it no longer depends on a coin step
follow_ups.why: The whole first-session simplification depends on this sim change; nothing today lets a harvested crop go back in the ground.

follow_ups.title: Spec the wordless 'storage full, time to sell' signal
follow_ups.first_action: Once the excess number is fixed, extend the existing basket-pip pattern into an overflow state rather than adding a new gauge
follow_ups.why: The HUD already has the right shape (pips that stop counting past five); it just needs pointing at the new trigger.

recommend.question: Should an actual written letter ever deliver a shipment or unlock, anywhere in the game?
recommend.answer: No — every arrival stays wordless, reusing the locked-icon-lights-up and single-highlight vocabulary already shipped; nothing mechanical needs a sentence.
recommend.why: The pre-reader rule already forbids required reading in the core loop, and the studio has already solved this exact problem three times without words.
recommend.instead: If he wants a supplier's voice for flavor, put it in an optional, adult-facing log a pre-reader never has to open — never in the required path.

check.summary: Sam's reading holds up against the docs and code — days 1–2 already skip the shop, the seed-from-harvest fork is named in the onboarding chapter, and the five-pip basket exists — but the reply overstates two small things the follow-up owners should know before building.

findings.what: The basket pips Sam calls 'already in the HUD' are treatment B's draft, only drawn when that treatment is on, and the five-pip cap is tagged as a playtest guess
findings.fix: The tier-0 'storage full' item should say it is promoting a draft treatment to the shipped HUD, not repointing something live; settle the treatment before the excess number

findings.what: The onboarding chapter does not just 'turn down' seed-from-harvest — it names it as the fallback and calls it cheap to switch to, which makes the doc change a promotion of a planned fallback rather than a reversal
findings.fix: Milo's note should cite the fallback clause and record the no-soft-lock property at lines 702-704 as still required under the new model

findings.what: The recommendation claims the studio has solved wordless unlocks 'three times'; the reply itself names two mechanisms (darkened locked icon, single glow), and nothing was counted
findings.fix: Drop the number or name the third case; the claim stands fine on the two
